utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning counsel, everyone in the courtroom. Mark Harmon, Lorna Bolton and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Appearing for Mr. Perisic today, Ms. Tina Drolec; Chad Mair; our intern, Alex Fielding; and Novak Lukic, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Good morning, Mr. Krayishnik. Just to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. May the record show in -- I think we didn't say so yesterday, that we are still sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis and we have been doing so since Monday. At least for this week. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krayishnik, I don't know if your head set is set to Serbian?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Then we'll continue as yesterday with the same caution, please wait a few seconds after my question. Please follow the text on the screen. When you see the typing has finished, you can start with your answer. I stopped yesterday because Ms. Bolton objected to my presenting a prior statement of the witness, that's where we left off. I was about to present the witness an answer he gave to the Prosecution in his first interview. Let me just refresh your memory a little. Yesterday, we discussed the fact that in your first interview, you had not had the opportunity to review all the notes and photographs and video footage that you saw before the second interview, and in the first interview, I mean in August this year, you said certain things that you later corrected, things that you stated to the best of your recollection based only on your memory. And then you said on that occasion you did not travel with Colonel Salapura and then you corrected that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now read out part of this answer, Your Honours. I will be reading this part that begins with this page in line 9, and in English it begins in line 20. Ms. Bolton's question reads --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Lukic, when you say beginning with this page, which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the page, to be precise, in B/C/S 15, and in English it's page 21. I'm starting to read from line 20. We will also later turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, do you see in English line 18, Ms. Bolton's question? It's in front of you, Witness. The transcript reads --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, I don't see this number 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Serbian it's line 9. I will read, you don't need to look at the screen. "Q. We were talking earlier about some of the people you met over there and your impressions of them. Do you recall meeting a Serbian general called Momcilo Perisic?" Your answer: "Yes, I met him once. "Q. Where was that?" Your answer: "That was in the headquarters with Mladic, yes, but only during the lunch hour, I think, and we had lunch there and we were on our way down to Pale. "Q. Did you speak much with him or ...?" Your answer: "No, actually I didn't talk to him at all. They were talking. They were sitting," and then something unintelligible, "and they were able to -- Ratko and all these important officers were behind our backs. I didn't have any conversation directly with them. " So this is a passage from the first statement you gave to Ms. Bolton in August, when you had not had the opportunity to see the photographs that later refreshed your memory; correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And during that first interview with Ms. Bolton --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Just one correction. Obviously my friend is reading from the B/C/S version and it's being translated into Court. The original interview was in English, and the wording of what was said about Ratko Mladic was slightly different in the actual English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It was important, not -- "big" not "important."

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, it was also: "... and Ratko and all those big," that was different, "army officers were all at our back." So it's a little different than: "They were sitting with their backs to us."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these are the problems we often have here. I agree with Ms. Bolton, the official version is in English. I read the official, or rather, the draft translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when you saw these photographs, you talked to Ms. Bolton again a month later in September, that's what I call the second interview, and when you saw the photographs, you remembered exactly how you were sitting and then you made the corrections you told us about yesterday; correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, asked by Ms. Bolton on page 9573, line 20 of the draft transcript of yesterday's session --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 43, line 16, if the Judges are looking at the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you didn't remember who Perisic was accompanied by when you first saw him outside that facility in Crna Rijeka; is that what you said to Ms. Bolton?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then Ms. Bolton read out to you yesterday in court part of your statement of September when, on page 9575, line 25, you said he was with General Mladic and General Gvero. Do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, this statement of September 2009 that Ms. Bolton read out to you, is not a statement that you gave to just anyone ten years ago, you gave it less than two months ago?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I noticed that speaking to the Court yesterday, you had forgotten what you had said to the Prosecutor two months ago, and the Prosecutor had to remind you; right?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could that have happened maybe because after 14 years you don't remember all these details what exactly happened, where you were, who exactly you talked to, what was said?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is true. That happened a long time ago. Since then I have not been thinking about it. I haven't revisited that. I did not imagine that I would have to go back to these events in my life that I had mostly forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These days you have been shown several video-clips, I'm talking only about what was done in the courtroom, and you were shown them at least on two occasions -- two more occasions, first in September, and then during proofing here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These video-clips were shown to you and you were asked to say to the best of your recollection whether during those days there had been any discussion about Srebrenica and the military operation around Srebrenica. The Prosecutor asked you that; correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation ] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we saw yesterday when this video footage was shown to you of 17 July 1995 in Han Pijesak --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me remind everyone that's the video-clip when Mladic is reading the list, the long list of names of donors.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At one point - that's page 12 of P2807, that's B/C/S transcript - he mentions that that was the day of the liberation of Srebrenica, the 17 of July, and he mentions the painter Milic od Macve?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember the reference to Milic od Macve or anything like that but I -- yes, that's the -- that is the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This event, the liberation of Srebrenica, is also mentioned in that video footage that shows your visit with Krajisnik and Karadzic of the 18th of July. One of the speakers then says they realise very well how important that event is, the liberation of Srebrenica, and how these people, Krajisnik and Karadzic, must be busy with all these activities.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These two video-clips were shown to you both in September, in your second interview with Ms. Bolton, and here in The Hague over the weekend?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And yesterday, on page 46 of the draft unrevised transcript, I couldn't identify it in the official one, Ms. Bolton read out to you part of your statement of September 2009 where you said that Mr. Mladic and Mr. Gvero, during this encounter outside that facility in Han Pijesak, sitting on those benches, were talking about Srebrenica in Perisic's presence. Do you remember the Prosecutor reading that passage to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, Ms. Bolton did not read out to you the proofing note of the 1st of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now place on the screen the document marked OTP Info Report 01112229. That's how it's marked in e-court. Those are the notes. Just a second. Ms. Drolec is helping us out as Case Manager today, to the best of her ability. I beg the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we get this document on the screen, during the interview Ms. Bolton had with you on the 1st of November, she made a note and you signed it. I'd like it to read out to you what the note says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, please. Can we call it up on the screen when we get the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see here in the third paragraph, that's the note made by

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: "[In English] Contrary to his information report of 18 September 2009 and his audio interview on the 9th of August 2009, today, the witness advised that he is not sure that the conversation about Srebrenica on 18th of July took place at the picnic area. It may have taken place in the boardroom." [Interpretation] Now, this is the note made by Ms. Bolton just a few days ago. She showed you that interview to which she referred yesterday in the courtroom and this note says that a few days ago you were not sure whether Srebrenica was discussed at all while they were sitting on those benches; correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So regardless of the fact that she presented to you your interview of September 2009 where you said that you had thought Srebrenica was discussed in that area with benches, where the photographs were made, just a few days ago, you told her you were not sure after all?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said that Madam Bolton reminded me that I signed the document, and I said I have a much better recollection of things that happened 20 or 30 years ago than things that happened two weeks or a month ago. And I feel that in my work; if I don't make a note of something, I forget it. That's why I keep in my cell phone a reminder of all the things I have to do, on which day, in order not to forget, because I did begin to forget. I don't know if it's age, probably is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You probably realise, Witness, that facts are very important to us here, and if you say that something happened, it's very important that you stand by it. And if you don't remember something, it's better to say, I don't remember it. That's very important in these proceedings. And I'm asking you once again, let's try to be as precise as possible. Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, I thought my -- before my friend moves on, I just want to correct part of the question that my friend asked at lines 10 to 13 of the transcript. He suggested there that what the witness said in his September 2009 statement was that he thought there had been discussion of Srebrenica, and the portion of the statement I put to him did not indicate -- was not equivocal, it indicated there was discussion. There was no use of the word that he "thought" it was discussed. So just indicating that I object to the suggestion that he was equivocal in his -- in paragraph 12 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand you. You are objecting to the use of the word "thought"?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your interview of September 2009 that Ms. Bolton read out yesterday you said that during that encounter, and let's be precise, I'm interested in the period when Mr. Perisic was present, that was 18 July, on the benches outside the building known as Javor. You said Mladic and Gvero discussed Srebrenica. That's written in paragraph 12 of the statement Ms. Bolton presented to you not only yesterday but during proofing a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you said to Ms. Bolton what I just read out, that you don't remember whether there was a discussion of Srebrenica on the benches or perhaps it was discussed in the boardroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw on video that Srebrenica was mentioned in that room?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you to answer with a yes, no, maybe, or I don't remember. At the time when you were sitting with Mr. Perisic --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't think it's appropriate for my friend to be telling the witness how he has to answer a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I only said something that is frequently said in courtrooms, that there are three answers to be expected from the witness. I don't see anything unusual about it. We always did that, especially when we wanted the witness to be concise. I really don't see a problem with telling the witness that he can answer yes, no, I don't know, or I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at that time when you were sitting with Mr. Perisic you heard discussion of Srebrenica? Yes, no, I don't remember, or I don't know.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was sitting with General Perisic and talked, I don't remember that we discussed, the two of us, I don't remember we discussed Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. In view of what you had said to Ms. Bolton that I just read out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Krayishnik, the question to you was: "When I was sitting with General Perisic and talked, I don't remember" -- I beg your pardon. "Do you remember that at that time when you were sitting with Mr. Perisic you heard discussion of Srebrenica?" Now, hearing a discussion of Srebrenica is one thing; you discussing with Mr. Perisic is another. The question is not whether you did discuss with Mr. Perisic. Did you hear a discussion about Srebrenica while you were sitting there, or don't you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understood your question but the question that was asked of me was whether I discussed with Mr. Perisic, and I answered I don't remember whether -- I don't remember that we discussed it, General Perisic and I. As to conversation around us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Look at page 10, line 24. Question by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this a question in Serbian or in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's in English, sir. The transcript before you is in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 10, line 24.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need assistance to find my way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I maybe read it in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I read it in English. He doesn't -- I would like him to see it himself because I read it out. He doesn't ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember whether I heard conversation, when I was sitting with Mr. Perisic, about Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krayishnik. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krayishnik, I won't take much longer, but I have to ask you a few more questions that follow from your evidence yesterday. You can't remember with certainty when, on the 17th of July, you arrived at Han Pijesak. You said yesterday -- you said so yesterday on page 9538, line 20, of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't know who organised vehicles for that journey, do you?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Neither do you know whether General Mladic mentioned Srebrenica several times -- several times those days when you were with him? That's on page 9551, line 1.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't remember what part of day it was, that footage when your group was handing over the medication and spare parts for cars in Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was on the 18th of July. That's not in dispute. But you said yesterday, on page 9557, line 8, that you don't know what part of day it was?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you can't remember either whether this video-clip about the hand-over of medication and spare parts was before or after your encounter with Mr. Perisic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can't remember where you spent that night of the 17th of July, you said that on 9557, line 17. You don't know where exactly in the area of Han Pijesak or Crna Rijeka. Your recollection of that day, 18 of July, 1995, is generally poor. It was 14 years ago and you can't remember much except what was shown you on photographs and video footage --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, is my friend testifying about indicating that his memory is generally poor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your friend's testifying, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I think my friend is testifying. He can ask a question if his memory is generally poor, but to be making the statement as part of his questions -- he says: "Your recollection of that day, 18 July, is generally poor," and then he goes on with a second question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. That is the problem with compound questions, with many sentences in one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, but before that, after my question on page 13, line 12, the witness's answer has not been recorded. No, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness's answer has not been recorded precisely because Madam Bolton objected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, apart from what you saw on photographs and video about the 18th of July, you can't remember other details because it was a long time ago and you don't have a good memory of that period long ago?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness another witness statement according to your guide-line 12, but we have to ask the witness to leave the courtroom for a moment because I have to tell you about the author of the text that I want to show the witness according to your guide-line 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't have to tell us about the author. Go ahead and ask the witness without telling him the author. You will tell us the author later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead, don't tell him who the author is, just ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay then, I'll do that later. But I thought I would perhaps put it on e-court for you so you could follow the passage I show the witness without the witness looking at it, because in that passage we can see whose talking. I have exact references in e-court of the pages I want to read to the witness. There are three references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you have -- on the exact pages you want to read, is the name of the witness mentioned there? Of the author?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In the header of each page you can see the name of the witness, and that's why I thought we could switch off the screen before the witness for awhile.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Before my friend does this, may I just have a brief indulgence to check something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Krayishnik, once again you are being asked to excuse us for a short while. If you can step out for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in keeping with your guide-lines, paragraph 12, I would like to show the witness now three brief passages from a statement Mr. Milan Lesic gave to Ms. Bolton on the 7th of August, 2009. These pages are in e-court and I can tell that you it's 213, 217, and 208. Those are the page numbers. I believe there's one more page, but these are the page numbers in e-court. The problem is -- it's easy to show it to you in e-court, but according to your guide-lines, you need to know exact references in the statement. Those pages have two numbers because the interview took two days. I would like to give you the reference for e-court. That would be the most precise way to go about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. And in fact, better still than giving us the reference, you can just show us the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, could my friend -- I have the print versions and could he tell me what pages he is referring to in the print versions of those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, and we were having trouble with that. That would be page 87.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, August 6th?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, second day, 7th August. Page 84 from line 15 to line 5 on page 85. Then on page 86, your question beginning with line 10 -- sorry, no, no, we are not going to take that one. Page 87, your question beginning on line 5 through line 30. Page 88, lines 10 through 15. And finally, page 79, lines 15 through line 5 on page 80. All this was in English. And now in e-court --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. This is the August 7th transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since there is a name on each page, I think that the witness shouldn't be allowed to see the screen. I think we can call the witness back into the courtroom. And as for e-court, I would like to call document 1D04 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you do that, Mr. Lukic, the document that has just disappeared from the screen, 01112229, what is supposed to become of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Line 15, Your Honours.

utterances.text: Question, starts a little bit somewhere between line 10 and 15: "You said that General Perisic was there for maybe two to three hours and that General Mladic told him that he had guests. utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's some confusion on the channels and I'm hearing both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.text: This is the part of the testimony -- of the interview with other person who now have to -- who now speaks about the same events which you testified, right? And I will, at the very end, when I finish reading this part of his interview, I will pose you some questions, okay? "Q. You said that General Perisic was there for maybe two to three hours, and that General Mladic told him that he had guests. Is that conversation you overheard?" "A. No. We were there sitting and he must have told him, he says: I'm having a guest, come on over. So he met all of us, as it shows in the tape." Ms. Bolton -- sorry, question: "So does General Perisic then call ahead and he says 'I have guests, come over,' or does he show up, drive up, and ... "A. I don't know that happened. "Q. Okay. No. We were sitting there, and the phone comes or something, and he just told us, Oh, General Perisic is coming over. "Q. And it was General Mladic who told you General Perisic is coming over? "A. And how long was it from the time he says General Perisic is coming over until he arrived? "A. Twenty minutes, ten minutes. Just having coffee and ..." This is the first part I read. Now I will read you the second part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: E-court, Your Honour, English page 219, line 1. I am starting to reading. B/C/S 218. Question -- 216, English, pardon. Just a second. Yes, thank you. From the very top.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Q. Okay. I assume that General Perisic and General Mladic -- was this just a social call, did he not have any time alone with General Mladic to discuss any business? "A. "Q. Okay. I know in your presence you're saying you don't think they did, but just so I'm clear -- "A. Yes. "Q. I'm asking you to remember something obviously that it's fourteen years ago now. "A. Yes. "Q. Would you be able to say you are a hundred per cent sure that the two of them never had the opportunity to speak privately that day? "A. That day I don't know, but not during my being there that I have seen them talking privately, no." Next -- on this page, my reference is now on line 10. "Q. And you don't recall there being a meal together or anything with General Perisic that day? "A. No, he did not eat with us that I remember it." And finally, I'm just wondering if you can put from the e-court for the others participating in the courtroom, the page English 280 -- 208 in the e-court. B/C/S 210, line 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, could we just --

Was there a meal or anything that he was present for or just ...? "A. No, he was just there to say hello to General Mladic, and he says, I have some visitors. And then first time I saw him and the last time I saw him. General Perisic, Momcilo Perisic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now go back to Serbian, could we set the witness's head set to channel 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As Ms. Bolton refreshed your memory with photographs and documents, I want to ask you something about what you just heard. As you could see, this was an interview between a certain person and the Prosecution about the same matters that have been discussed here. I want to know several things. Is it correct that you were sitting there with that group? Further, that Mr. Perisic joined you on those benches, three, that he sat with you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: One question at a time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard what this person said?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that this entire encounter happened in this way, that you were sitting there and then Mr. Perisic joined you on those benches; is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's a possibility. As I said earlier, and as I have to say again, it was a long time ago. Obviously my memory has deteriorated in the past four or five years. That's why I asked Ms. Bolton to let my wife accompany me here because I keep forgetting things. I forget to take my medicine, and if I don't take it regularly, I have real health problems. These are the facts. It's reality. Some things I remember, some things I forget, but obviously that witness has a better memory. He recalls these events better than I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That witness -- you didn't say that yesterday, but it was shown to you through references to previous interviews, that witness says that it was no luncheon, that you were just sitting talking?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's possible. Now that I heard part of his evidence, I keep thinking and I can't remember whether we had lunch there or at Pale, or whether we had lunch at all. And I don't remember the exact time when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Except on that occasion you have never seen General Momcilo Perisic either before or after that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krayishnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination. I don't wish to tender the part I read out as evidence because we have it in the transcript. We can keep it as a reserve until the witness appears in the courtroom with regard to your instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Madam Bolton, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I will have some re-examination, Your Honours. I see it's 10.00. I wonder if we could take the break earlier so that I can locate in the transcript some of the things -- questions Mr. Lukic asked today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We'll do that. We'll take a break, then come back at quarter to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, that would be plenty of time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Hello again, Mr. Krayishnik.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hello, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Today you told us that you take some medication, and I'd like to know what the medication you take -- what conditions it's to control?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm taking for diabetes [Realtime transcript read in error "arthritis"] and the cholesterol and some natural medication for all kind of body function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said diabetics, not arthritis.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as well, arthritis as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So diabetes, arthritis and cholesterol; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the fish oil, like for memories and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Omega 3, that kind of preventative stuff?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you take any medication for any kind of cognitive condition or psychiatric condition?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Any medication for your memory?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there is some of these medication for retaining memories.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What medication do you take to retain your memory?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's glucosamine, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Glucosamine?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and some other, I can't remember what the name. It's in a bottle.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Glucosamine is not a prescription medication; correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a natural doctor's prevent -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: It's something you can buy in the drugstore; correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually I buy it at the doctor's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You buy it at the doctor's office. Have you ever been diagnosed with any kind of a memory problem by any physician, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't, but I haven't been checked either.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Are you still employed, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm semi-retired.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you say you are semi-retired, who do you work for?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have an insurance agency and I am in association with insurance brokerage firm called Financial Horizon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you have employees, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part-time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how many different companies, insurance companies do you represent in your business?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's about 29 company in the list, but I deal about five, six companies, occasionally from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: How many days a week do you currently work, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of days a week.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Two days a week?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two, three, depends on the need.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Any idea what your annual revenues are for your company?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- from the insurance agency approximately around 30.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I also have income from my dealerships, silent partner.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You also have another business, then. A silent partner in a dealership of what?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: A dealership of vehicle, cars.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say annual revenues of about $30.000? Annual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And what would you bring in from your car dealership partnership?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my friend suggested to you, during questioning today, that essentially you have no memory of the discussions around July 16th, 17th and 18th except to the extent that your memory has been refreshed by the videos. Do you recall that line of questioning, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You've also conceded that the first time that you spoke to the Office of the Prosecutor in August 2009, that at that point in time your memory hadn't been refreshed by any video-tapes; correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think you had a couple of pictures or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: But no video-tapes; right?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I don't think we had video.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And I want to remind you, sir, then, what your memory was before it was refreshed from the video-tapes about this discussion and meeting with Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm looking at the transcript of that audio interview, which is ID number 1D04-0476. If we could look at page -- what I have as page 21. If that could be displayed, please. So page 21 in the English version, please. Could you --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You see at the bottom, I want to read you the following passage starting in e-court at line -- line 18. I asked you: "We were talking earlier about some of the people you met over there and your impressions of them. Do you recall meeting a Serbian general called Momcilo Perisic?" And you responded: "Yes, I met him once." I asked: "Where was that?" You responded: "And that was in a headquarters with Mladic, yeah, but only with the lunch hour, I think, and we had lunch there and we were on our way down to Pale." And I asked: "Did you speak much with him or ...?" And you started and said: "No, actually" - if we could turn the page please - "I didn't talk to him at all. They were talking -- they were sitting up," then there's something we can't hear, "and they could -- and Ratko and all those big army officers were all at our back. I didn't have any conversation directly with them." And I said: "Okay. Do you remember which trip this was or ...?" And you said: "I think that was 1995, when they liberated the Srebrenica." Second passage I want to put to you is in that same transcript --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: My apologies. If we could have page 31. Could I have -- my pages aren't the same as in e-court, could I have page 32, please. If we could scroll to the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. We are talking earlier on the page about Naser Oric and the raiding parties, and then starting at approximately line 27 in e-court, Mr. Nicholls was asking you questions. And he said: "And were they discussing that at the lunch that" --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Actually, I'm sorry, could we scroll up? I need to start this passage a little earlier to give it context. Yes, thank you, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: This is what you said: "Well, apparently it was a major victory for them because apparently there were soldiers going over constantly. They were going and shooting the Serbian villagers and Serbian people that were," THEN there's something inaudible, "they were -- that group was never kind of safe." Mr. Nicholls said: "Naser Oric?" And you said: "Yeah." I said: "Raiding parties of Srebrenica?" And you said: "Yeah, yeah, yeah. And ..." And Mr. Nicholls said: "And so ..." And you said: "That was it. But I thought that they were, like, much more safe then," and there's something indiscernible. Mr. Nicholls said: "And were they discussing that at that lunch that, you know, now it's over, that problem? I mean, it's liberated, that problem is done?" And you said: "Yeah, and they did say that they liberated and they were -- but I -- they didn't spend very much time on it. They were -- I don't think they had time at all. They just -- lunch" --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could turn the page. If we could scroll up. In English. If we could scroll to the top of the page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: "Yeah, and they did say -- and that's what I said. I think I saw General Perisic was there as well, and I think that he didn't spend time with him much except lunch. "Do you recall who was talking about Srebrenica that time or ...? "Well, Gvero, Mladic, and they were laughing about it, that they liberated," something inaudible. I asked: "Was General Perisic there to hear about that?" You said: "I think he would hear it because they were all there." So, sir, before your memory -- you had any opportunity to view the videos, when first mention was made of General Perisic, you immediately said you remember that the occasion that you met him was on the liberation of Srebrenica, and then you went on to say there was discussion of Srebrenica at that lunch in the presence of General Perisic. Do you recall that conversation, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: With you. Yes, I do recall the conversation with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, and Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Correct. Now, you then gave a signed statement to the Office of the Prosecutor dated September 10th, 2009.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And this is 1D04-0461.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All these IDs are not being tendered?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: They have not been tendered as yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And they are not intended to be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I am not intending to tender them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You then --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, if I could have the English version, and I'll be looking at paragraph 21. If we could focus in a little bit, it's a very hard to read. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You then gave a statement in September 2009 that you've already told us you read before signing, where you indicated: "We were with Generals Mladic, Perisic, and Gvero at the picnic table for a couple of hours. As I stated in my previous statement, Generals Gvero and Mladic were discussing the liberation of Srebrenica at lunch. They did not spend much time on it. General Perisic was present to hear this conversation. There were no signs of disagreement between the generals. There was a lot of joking around at lunch." So again in that statement, sir, you were unequivocal about the fact that there had been this discussion in General Perisic's presence on July 18th. And I'd like to know, sir, why it is now, today, in responding to questions from Mr. Lukic that you are now no longer sure? What has happened in the last month and a half?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I have heard all kind of and seen all kind of pictures and because this was so long and going back and forth refreshing my memories and discussions, and I seen that I may assume some of these things through my memory. And even at that time, like I said, that I wasn't sure of a lot of these things. And also --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Well, could --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Mr. Lukic suggested those pictures did refresh some of my memories. And even here you show me more picture than I didn't see it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, first of all, yesterday you testified that there was this discussion. So what have you seen between yesterday and today in terms of photographs or videos that have changed your mind?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not I changed my mind. When we were talking about the lunch, I actually meant when we were sitting at the table where we had the lunch before, and I am not sure if we had lunch that day there or not. I cannot recall exactly and say that I'm a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I do remember that table outside in the picnic area, that we were sitting there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So it's the fact that you are not sure whether or not you had lunch that's changed your mind as to whether or not this conversation about this major victory at Srebrenica in the presence of a Serbian army general took place?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that, but also I think those pictures, I think all these pictures that different people sitting at different places and sitting with different people, that made me kind of more confused and unsure of a lot of these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: But those pictures were shown to you yesterday before you were asked the questions about the conversation at Srebrenica and then yesterday you indicated that that conversation did take place?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I'm saying, after seeing these pictures that you show me in the last four days and some pictures that you show me on, I believe, was September 9th, these pictures, they were refreshing some of my memories and confusing me at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So what pictures have you been shown here that you weren't shown before you signed your statement in September 2009?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was -- yesterday was shown a lot of pictures that I don't remember seeing them before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sitting outside and inside and General Mladic on the telephone, and the pictures that you were showing me these, I believe, was the last picture with brother Rakanovic in the room that also refreshed my memory that I wasn't there at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. So that footage with Gorazde is something that you remember not seeing before. The photographs at the picnic table, are you saying that you did not see those during proofing or -- sorry, when we met in September, and those are the photos at the picnic area from July 19th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't remember did I see all of those pictures or not when I was meeting with you in Milton on September 9th.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. If I could refresh your memory, sir, from paragraph 15 of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could go back.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You'll see a list of --

utterances.text: Sir, then --
